title: A Theory for Record Linkage
abstract: Develops a probabilistic framework for deciding whether pairs of records refer to the same person, object, or event. It formalizes link, non-link, and possible-link decisions while controlling false-link and missed-link error rates, providing a foundational model for evidence combination under uncertain identity.
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

title: A Method for Calibrating False-Match Rates in Record Linkage
abstract: Addresses how to choose a record-linkage cutoff after records have been assigned agreement weights. It models observed weights as a mixture of true-match and false-match distributions and estimates the false-match rate associated with alternative thresholds, explicitly supporting controlled identity decisions.
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

title: Cross-Document Event Coreference: Annotations, Experiments, and Observations
abstract: Presents early work on identifying mentions of the same event across different documents, including cross-document event-coreference annotations and experiments. It is a foundational study of event identity across document boundaries rather than ordinary within-document reference resolution.

title: Taking Email to Task: The Design and Evaluation of a Task Management Centered Email Tool
abstract: Describes Taskmaster, an email system designed around the observation that workplace email frequently functions as a task-management environment. The interface reorganizes messages and associated resources around work tasks and was evaluated using participants' live email, providing enterprise-communication evidence about persistent task-oriented organization even though it does not establish an automated cross-thread identity benchmark.

title: Relational clustering for multi-type entity resolution
abstract: Studies entity resolution when records are connected by heterogeneous relations. The method combines attribute similarity with relational evidence and performs collective clustering, illustrating how links among surrounding objects can contribute evidence for or against an identity decision.

title: A Latent Dirichlet Model for Unsupervised Entity Resolution
abstract: Presents a probabilistic unsupervised model for resolving records into latent entities. The formulation combines multiple observed attributes rather than relying on a single similarity signal and treats identity assignments as uncertain latent structure.
venue: SIAM International Conference on Data Mining

title: A hybrid learning system for recognizing user tasks from desktop activities and email messages
abstract: Develops a system for associating a knowledge worker's computer activities and email messages with persistent user-defined tasks. The approach combines learned task recognition with information from multiple desktop resources, making it relevant to cross-application work-instance association rather than merely classifying generic activity types.
venue: International Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces

title: Collective entity resolution in relational data
abstract: Introduces collective entity resolution that uses both record attributes and relationships among records and entities. Resolution decisions are made jointly so that inferred identities and relational evidence can reinforce one another, providing a transferable model for combining multiple evidence sources in identity clustering.
venue: ACM Transactions on Knowledge Discovery from Data

title: Online Collective Entity Resolution
abstract: Extends collective entity resolution to an online setting where resolution is performed as new queries or records arrive. It exploits relational evidence while avoiding full recomputation, making it relevant to incremental identity assignment in a growing stream.

title: Nonparametric Bayesian Models for Unsupervised Event Coreference Resolution
abstract: Applies nonparametric Bayesian models to unsupervised event-coreference resolution and evaluates both within-document and cross-document event identity. The models infer event clusters rather than requiring a fixed number of identities in advance.
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems

title: Unsupervised Event Coreference Resolution with Rich Linguistic Features
abstract: Studies open-domain event coreference using unsupervised models and rich linguistic features. It evaluates clustering of mentions that refer to the same events and examines evidence beyond lexical similarity, including contextual and semantic information.

title: Event correlation for process discovery from Web service interaction logs
abstract: Addresses correlation of events generated by enterprise applications and Web services when traces are scattered across systems and explicit process-instance identifiers are unavailable. The method determines which events belong to the same execution instance so that business processes can be discovered from distributed logs.

title: Controlling false match rates in record linkage using extreme value theory
abstract: Develops a record-linkage thresholding method aimed specifically at controlling false matches. Extreme-value modeling is used to estimate an appropriate decision threshold without requiring a labeled training set, providing transferable evidence for conservative identity assignment and false-link control.

title: Semantic Relations between Events and their Time, Locations and Participants for Event Coreference Resolution
abstract: Examines how event components such as time, location, participants, and other semantic relations contribute to deciding whether event mentions are coreferential. The work directly investigates compatibility evidence that can establish or reject same-event identity rather than relying only on trigger similarity.

title: Evaluation for Partial Event Coreference
abstract: Distinguishes full event identity from partial event coreference such as subevent and membership relations. It represents partial coreference as directed hierarchical event structure and develops evaluation metrics for systems that predict those structures, explicitly demonstrating that event relations need not be a simple equivalence partition.
venue: Second Workshop on EVENTS: Definition, Detection, Coreference, and Representation

title: Unsupervised Event Coreference Resolution
abstract: Develops unsupervised probabilistic approaches for grouping mentions that refer to the same events. The work models event identity using rich linguistic evidence and evaluates event-coreference clustering without requiring supervised coreference labels during training.

title: A Hierarchical Distance-dependent Bayesian Model for Event Coreference Resolution
abstract: Introduces a hierarchical distance-dependent Bayesian model for event coreference that jointly captures mention-level and cluster-level information. The model performs event clustering without fixing the number of event identities in advance and uses dependencies among mentions to improve identity decisions.
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Event Coreference Resolution by Iteratively Unfolding Inter-dependencies among Events
abstract: Builds event clusters iteratively while exploiting dependencies within and across event chains. It uses different classifiers for within-document and cross-document links and, after cluster merges, combines arguments from the merged events so that accumulated evidence affects later identity decisions.

title: Cross-Document, Cross-Language Event Coreference Annotation Using Event Hoppers
abstract: Develops cross-document and cross-language event-coreference annotation using event hoppers. The annotation framework deliberately supports an inclusive conception of coreference and discusses the evidence annotators use when deciding whether event mentions across documents and languages belong to the same event hopper.

title: New Insights into Cross-Document Event Coreference: Systematic Comparison and a Simplified Approach
abstract: Systematically compares approaches to cross-document event coreference and analyzes which modeling choices materially affect performance. It proposes a simplified approach while retaining the task's explicit target of clustering mentions that denote the same real-world event.

title: Event Coreference Resolution with their Paraphrases and Argument-aware Embeddings
abstract: Improves event-coreference resolution by incorporating paraphrase information and argument-aware event representations. The approach is relevant to continuity expressed with different wording because it explicitly predicts event identity while using arguments to disambiguate otherwise similar event descriptions.

title: Fast Bayesian Record Linkage With Record-Specific Disagreement Parameters
abstract: Develops probabilistic record linkage with record-specific disagreement probabilities, improving decisions when common attribute values make identities ambiguous. The method is evaluated against expert-labeled matches and also provides ways to estimate true-positive rate and positive predictive value when full ground truth is unavailable.

title: Confidence Calibration for Domain Generalization under Covariate Shift
abstract: Studies confidence calibration when deployment data differ from training data through covariate shift. It investigates how calibration information from multiple source domains can generalize to unseen target domains, providing transfer evidence for confidence thresholds under distribution change.

title: Post-Hoc Uncertainty Calibration for Domain Drift Scenarios
abstract: Investigates post-hoc confidence calibration when the test distribution drifts away from the calibration distribution. The method perturbs validation data to improve uncertainty estimates under domain shift, providing transferable evidence that IID calibration alone is insufficient for changing streams.

title: Cross-document Event Identity via Dense Annotation
abstract: Directly studies the identity of textual events across different documents and argues that earlier annotation schemes insufficiently address event identity and quasi-identity. Its dense annotation workflow records coreference links together with overlapping contexts such as time, location, and participants, enabling analysis of how those evidence dimensions relate to identity judgments.

title: FIRLA: a Fast Incremental Record Linkage Algorithm
abstract: Addresses incremental record linkage in which previously clustered identities must be updated as new records arrive. FIRLA reuses prior linkage output and restricts unnecessary comparisons, making it relevant to maintaining identity state incrementally rather than recomputing a complete static clustering.

title: Improving Accuracy and Explainability in Event-Case Correlation via Rule Mining
abstract: Studies event correlation when business-process events lack unique case identifiers and therefore must be grouped into process instances. It introduces rule mining to improve correlation accuracy and explainability, targeting explicit event-to-case identity rather than assuming a correct case ID is already supplied.
venue: IEEE International Conference on Process Mining

title: Event Coreference Resolution for Contentious Politics Events
abstract: Creates and analyzes a multilingual, multi-source event-coreference dataset for contentious-politics events and measures the contribution of event-coreference resolution to event information collection. The study highlights how separate documents can provide erroneous or partial information about events unless mentions of the same underlying event are resolved together.

title: Event-case correlation for process mining using probabilistic optimization
abstract: Addresses business-process event logs in which case identifiers are missing and event records must be assigned to the process instances that generated them. It formulates event-to-case correlation as a probabilistic optimization problem using process-model and data constraints, directly modeling the choice among competing case identities.

title: Step-by-Step Case ID Identification Based on Activity Connection for Cross-Organizational Process Mining
abstract: Studies case identification for cross-organizational process mining where different organizations use independent identifier systems. It incrementally identifies probable case-ID correspondences using connections among activities, providing business-workflow evidence for correlating records that belong to the same distributed process instance.

title: CorefPrompt: Prompt-based Event Coreference Resolution by Measuring Event Type and Argument Compatibilities
abstract: Recasts event-coreference resolution as a prompt-based prediction problem and adds explicit auxiliary judgments for event-type compatibility and argument compatibility. These compatibility signals expose part of the evidence used to decide whether two mentions denote the same real-world event rather than relying only on opaque mention encodings.

title: Selective Classification Under Distribution Shifts
abstract: Extends selective classification, in which a model may abstain instead of making an unreliable prediction, to deployment under distribution shift. The generalized framework considers in-distribution, label-shifted or out-of-distribution, and covariate-shifted samples and evaluates confidence scores for risk-aware rejection.

title: Convergence Diagnostics for Entity Resolution
abstract: Reviews Bayesian entity-resolution models that infer partitions of records while quantifying uncertainty and focuses on whether posterior computation has actually converged. The paper is relevant to identity-state reliability because it emphasizes uncertainty in partitions and warns that apparently stable identity assignments may reflect poor inference rather than evidence.
venue: Annual Review of Statistics and Its Application

title: Synergetic Event Understanding: A Collaborative Approach to Cross-Document Event Coreference Resolution with Large Language Models
abstract: Combines an LLM that produces comprehensive event summaries with a task-specific smaller model that learns event representations for cross-document coreference. The approach is evaluated on clustering mentions that denote the same real-world events and is intended to improve robustness to complex and diverse cross-document contexts.

title: Improving cross-document event coreference resolution by discourse coherence and structure
abstract: Addresses the lack of coherent shared context between event mentions in different documents. It selects sentences to construct coherent cross-document context, represents that context with discourse structure, and uses the resulting global interaction evidence to resolve event identity; experiments are reported on ECB+ and GVC.

title: Hypergraph convolutional networks with multi-ordering relations for cross-document event coreference resolution
abstract: Represents events and their related elements in hypergraphs so that higher-order relationships can contribute to cross-document coreference decisions. Hypergraph convolution is used to aggregate complex relational evidence before pair scoring and clustering of mentions into same-event groups.

title: Conformal selective prediction with cost aware deferral for safe clinical triage under distribution shift
abstract: Combines selective prediction with conformal methods and cost-aware deferral under distribution shift. Although evaluated in clinical triage rather than workplace communication, it provides transferable evidence for allowing uncertain cases to be deferred instead of forcing an identity-like classification when confidence is unreliable.
